items.claim: Anonymous or guest access to an SMB share, and the enumeration that reveals it, is the usual route to credentials or a file drop on a Windows target.
items.body:
In practice on HTB this shows up as: | `smbclient -N -L //10.129.14.128` | Null-session testing against the SMB service. |
| `smbmap -H 10.129.14.128` | Network share enumeration using `smbmap`. |
| `smbmap -H 10.129.14.128 -r notes` | Recursive network share enumeration using `smbmap`. |
| `smbmap -H 10.129.14.128 --download "notes\note.txt"` | Download a specific file from the shared folder. |

Write-up provenance: Esther7171/HackTheBox-Writeups-Walkthroughs :: Write-ups/Academy/04. Exploitation/19. Attacking Common Services/Attacking Common Services.md (1121 words, classified network).
items.disproof: Refuted when the share requires authentication and rejects guest/anonymous sessions, and no share permits a write, so the share yields neither credentials nor a file drop.
